receiver: whoever maintains the tool, a person or an AI, and whoever builds its preview run to these tests
use: trusting from these tests passing that showing the planned moves does what docs/ux.md says, and building the preview run until they pass

questions.question: Which oldest Python 3 version must the tool and its tests run on? docs/architecture.md says only 'Python 3', so B-1 (nothing newer than the oldest version named) has no version to check the tests against, and pyproject.toml will need the same floor.
questions.recommended: Python 3.9, because it is the python3 that macOS gives with its own command line tools, so a macOS user can run the tool and its tests without installing another Python.

questions.question: May mutation testing and coverage measurement be left out of the tests, with a comment in tests/test_preview.py saying the user decided so and why? The development rules name the standard library alone and no coverage or mutation tool, and B-6 asks either such checks or a written decision of the user for leaving them out; property tests can still be made with Python's own random module.
questions.recommended: Yes, leave them out with that comment, because adding coverage.py or mutmut would change the development rules in docs/architecture.md, which this task does not make, while property tests with random and cases from each partition and reason of docs/ux.md still hold every preview behavior.
